title: Product sense & metrics | LLM evaluation
objectives: Answer metric-definition and metric-drop cases with structure. Build evaluations you can trust: the skill that most directly bridges the two tracks.
exercise: Read 50 traces from your Week 6 RAG bot, build a failure taxonomy, write two code assertions and one LLM judge, and measure the judge's agreement with your own labels. Separately, talk through three full metric-drop cases out loud and record yourself.
resources: Google DS interview guides (Interview Query, Exponent, DataInterview)

cards.q: Propose a North Star and two guardrails for GrabFood's group-order feature.
cards.answer: North Star: completed group orders per week (or the share of eligible sessions that complete a group order), reflecting value delivered to groups. Guardrails: delivery time / late-delivery rate, cancellation or refund rate, merchant prep-time SLA, and cannibalisation of total order GMV per user.
rubric: North Star reflects value delivered (completed group orders), not vanity
Two sensible guardrails (delivery time, cancellations/refunds, cannibalisation, merchant SLA)

cards.q: A good North Star metric…
choices: Captures core user value and leads long-term business outcomes
Is whatever moved most last quarter

cards.q: Order the metric hierarchy from top to bottom.
items: Guardrail metrics that must not regress

cards.q: For a digital wallet, which is the better North Star?
Input metrics are useful because…
choices: Teams can move them directly, and they drive the North Star

cards.q: Why is 'time in app' a risky success metric for a payments product?
cards.answer: In payments, a good experience is fast and frictionless. More time can mean confusion, failed payments or retries. The metric rewards the wrong behaviour (it's easy to game and misaligned with user value). Prefer successful payment rate, time-to-pay, or repeat usage.
rubric: Fast = good for payments; more time can mean friction

cards.q: A metric is 'sensitive' if…
choices: It moves detectably when the product meaningfully changes

cards.q: Why is 30-day revenue a hard primary metric for a 2-week test?
choices: Low sensitivity / not observable in the window: noisy and lagging; use a validated leading proxy

cards.q: Goodhart's law in metric design means…
choices: When a measure becomes a target, it stops being a good measure
Metrics always regress to the mean

cards.q: A metric is 'attributable' when…
choices: Changes can be traced to a specific product change or team

cards.q: Put the metric-drop diagnosis steps in order.
items: Check external factors (seasonality, holidays, competitors, outages)

cards.q: Daily payments drop 15% overnight, only on Android, starting with the latest app release. First suspect?
choices: The release: a tracking or payment-flow bug in that Android version

cards.q: Why check instrumentation first?
choices: Many 'drops' are logging/pipeline changes, not real behaviour, and it's cheap to rule out

cards.q: Conversion rate fell, but conversions are flat and traffic rose 20% from a new ad channel. Likely explanation?
choices: Mix shift: new low-intent traffic dilutes the rate; segment by channel

cards.q: Simpson's paradox in a metric drop means…
choices: A trend in every segment reverses in the aggregate because the segment mix changed (e.g. every segment improved, yet the total fell)

cards.q: Conversion +2% but refunds +5%. Launch? What else do you need?
cards.answer: Don't decide on percentages alone. Net it out in absolute terms: incremental profit = extra conversions × margin − extra refunds × (refund cost + ops + fraud signal). Check whether refunds are concentrated in a segment (fraud, a specific merchant) and are significant, and whether there are long-term effects (trust, chargebacks, repeat purchase). Decide against pre-agreed guardrail thresholds. Possibly launch with a fix or ramp a subset.
rubric: Guardrail thresholds / launch criteria agreed in advance

cards.q: Primary metric improved significantly; a guardrail degraded beyond its threshold. Default decision?
choices: Don't ship as-is; investigate and fix the guardrail regression
Rerun until the guardrail is neutral

cards.q: The result is flat with a tight CI around zero, and the feature adds maintenance cost. Decision?
choices: Usually don't ship: no measurable benefit and a real cost

cards.q: Why agree launch criteria before the experiment?
choices: To prevent post-hoc rationalisation of whatever result appears

cards.q: A dark-pattern subscription flow raises sign-ups 10%. Main concern?
choices: Short-term gain vs long-term trust, churn, complaints and regulatory risk

cards.q: Why do the error analysis yourself before writing any automated evaluator?
cards.answer: You don't know the real failure modes until you read traces. Generic metrics measure the wrong things. Reading traces (open coding → grouping into a taxonomy) reveals the app-specific failures worth measuring, and it grounds evaluator criteria and judge prompts in reality. Automating before understanding builds evaluators for imagined problems.
rubric: Failure modes are app-specific and discovered empirically

cards.q: Order the error-analysis workflow.
items: Collect a diverse sample of traces
Open coding: write free-form notes on what went wrong
Axial coding: group notes into failure categories
Count frequency of each failure mode
Prioritise and build evaluators for the top modes

cards.q: In open coding, you should note…
choices: The first/most upstream error you see in each trace, in your own words

cards.q: No production traffic yet. How do you get traces?
choices: Generate synthetic queries across chosen dimensions (persona, intent, difficulty) and run them

cards.q: When do you stop reading traces in a round?
choices: When new traces stop revealing new failure categories (theoretical saturation)

cards.q: Give one reason pass/fail judgments are more actionable than 1–5 scores.
cards.answer: Binary forces a clear definition of acceptable. It's more consistent between annotators and judges, and it maps directly to 'fix this or not'. Likert midpoints (is it a 3 or a 4?) are noisy, hard to calibrate and need larger samples to detect change.

cards.q: Which check suits a code-based assertion rather than an LLM judge?
choices: Output is valid JSON with all required fields and amount > 0

cards.q: Best design for an LLM-judge evaluator?
choices: One specific failure mode per judge, binary pass/fail with a written critique
The same model grading itself with no rubric

cards.q: Why are ROUGE/BERTScore weak evals for an LLM assistant?
choices: They measure surface/semantic overlap with a reference, not task-specific correctness; many good answers differ from the reference

cards.q: Prefer code-based checks over LLM judges when possible because they are…
Your judge agrees with humans 95% of the time, but failures are only 5% of the data. What should you check instead?
choices: TPR/TNR (recall on the failure class and on the pass class)
cards.explain: A judge that always says 'pass' gets 95% agreement.

cards.q: 100 human-labelled traces: 20 fails, 80 passes. The judge flags 16 of the 20 fails and 8 of the 80 passes. TPR on failures (in %)?
How should you split labelled data when developing a judge prompt?
choices: Train (few-shot examples) / dev (iterate) / test (final unbiased estimate)
Use all labels for few-shot examples
Test on the same examples used in the prompt

cards.q: Known LLM-judge bias in pairwise comparisons?
choices: Position bias (favouring the first or second answer) and verbosity bias

cards.q: Your judge's raw failure rate on production is 10%, with known TPR/TNR. What can you do?
choices: Correct the observed rate for judge error to estimate the true failure rate (with a CI)

cards.q: Define faithfulness vs answer relevance.
cards.answer: Faithfulness (groundedness): every claim in the answer is supported by the retrieved context, with no hallucinated content. Answer relevance: the answer actually addresses the user's question. An answer can be faithful but irrelevant, or relevant but unfaithful.

cards.q: To evaluate the retriever separately from the generator, measure…
choices: Recall@k / MRR against labelled relevant documents per query

cards.q: Evals in CI vs production monitoring?
choices: CI: fixed test set gating changes before deploy; production: sample live traces to detect new failures and drift
CI only for code, never prompts

cards.q: Faithful but low relevance suggests…
choices: Retrieval returned off-topic context, or the prompt didn't focus on the question

cards.q: Your RAG eval set should include…
choices: Answerable, unanswerable (should abstain) and ambiguous queries
Only questions the model already gets right
